title: More clearly distinguish authoring conformance requirements

labels.name: a11y-needs-resolution
labels.description: Issue the Accessibility Group has raised and looks for a response on.

body:
About once a month I get a question from browser engineers who are confused by the spec into thinking that authoring conformance requirements govern their implementation. E.g. this week I got folks confused that the spec didn't say how to handle non-UTF8 `<meta charset>` (because that is hidden in the parser section, whereas the `<meta>` element section contains authoring requirements) and folks not realizing the difference between [valid `<link sizes>` values](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-sizes) and [the `<link sizes>` parser](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#rel-icon:attr-link-sizes-2).

I think that we should consider a light touch of styling to help with this. I don't have any great ideas. In my head it's a very-light-yellow background that, when hovered over, has a little popup saying "Authoring requirement ([?](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/introduction.html#how-to-read-this-specification))" or something. (I tried to make this work for 5 minutes in devtools and it didn't look right. Probably a more concerted effort could produce something.) Note that it needs to be sentence-level, not paragraph level, e.g. in [the `<link sizes>` attribute definition](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-sizes) the first three sentences are general but the rest of the paragraph contains authoring requirements.

If we agree on the styling here then I'd be interested in taking on the effort of marking up all the conformance requirements appropriately.
